question: Ergometrine (ergot alkaloid) is a safe and appropriate second-line uterotonic for postpartum haemorrhage in a patient with severe pre-eclampsia and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Ergometrine is absolutely contraindicated in any patient with hypertension, pre-eclampsia, or eclampsia. Administering it in this context can precipitate a life-threatening hypertensive crisis. This is one of the most important contraindication traps in obstetric pharmacology.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. Ergometrine is CONTRAINDICATED in hypertension, pre-eclampsia, and cardiovascular disease. It causes sustained vasoconstriction and can precipitate a hypertensive crisis or stroke. Use carboprost, misoprostol, or Syntometrine with extreme caution; in hypertensive patients, escalate to carboprost (if no asthma) or surgical options.
